authorSelfScore.scorer: author self-score (the authoring agent; not the independent score create-rigged-character-assets requires)
gaps: Ruby jewels on the shoulder and thigh bosses are brass caps: the 4-material budget (two shared brass sets, gunmetal, hound-glow) and no vertex colours leave no red material.
Glow reads peach rather than hot orange in the Blender compare at the project's GLOW_STRENGTH 0.7 convention; the grille and side lenses are less luminous than the concept.
Front view: the skull reads narrower and much darker than the concept's broad lit face, and the eye slits are small from the front; the ears read as upturned flaps rather than folded rose ears.

Forelegs are plated cylinders with a gunmetal wrist joint and a short angled pastern; the concept's forearm plate is a more sculpted taper with engraved panels, and its far-side legs are staggered while the model's rest stance is symmetric.
Front view chest is a single smooth bulb with the grille low on the prow; the concept's cuirass carries more plate seams, rivets and engraved panel lines everywhere.
Paws are simpler than the concept's arched, individually jointed toes.
authorSelfScore.method: Author self-score from spring-hound.fidelity-compare.jpg: orthographic Blender renders of the low-poly model at the concept's side, front and back angles, framed at the concept's own metres per pixel (side 1.2 m / 855 px, front/back 1.21 m / 875 px), judged side by side and by 50/50 overlay. Supporting silhouette IoU against background-thresholded masks (difference > 22 from the corner colour, 5 px median): side 0.43, front 0.33, back 0.23. The IoU understates the match: the polished skull and gunmetal parts render near the background tone head-on and drop out of the render mask, and the painted concept's soft shading and far-side legs inflate its mask. The compare lighting is the fixed warden-matched rig and was not tuned to the score.

independentScore.scorer: independent reviewer agent (separate from the authoring agent; did not build the model)

rubric.note: Unchanged geometry, unchanged score. The side view keeps the long low body, coil spine and key tail. The legs are straight plated tubes without the concept's angled hocks and tapered forearm plates. The head is a long flat crocodile snout with a spatulate lower jaw instead of the concept's short greyhound skull, and head-on the ears flare up and out like horns rather than folding as rose ears.

Coil spine, neck coils, winding key on a segmented tail and hinged toothed jaw are all present. The eye slits now read as lit amber slits head-on (#F0A235 and #F4B743), which is the gain since 61. The chest is still wrong against the concept: the concept front shows one bright grille core, while the model shows two round side lenses that out-shine and out-size it. The lenses measure value 0.96 to 0.98 (#F5B741, #FAD04E); the grille core reads 0.80 in its brightest gaps (#CB963D) and 0.60 between bars (#996A39). The ruby bosses are still brass caps.

Unchanged. Plates separate cleanly over gunmetal joints but are smooth, with none of the concept's engraved panel lines, seams or rivets. The hammered normal reads as noise, and the paws are simplified blocks. In the engine shot the chest bulb carries a blown specular patch (#FBF1DE, saturation 0.12) that reads as a white spot.

Fixed: the glow is now saturated amber. Glow pixels in the after crop of p6-glow-before-after.jpg have a median of #F5B140 (hue 39, saturation 0.74), against #C68D5C peach at the same pixels before. That matches the art bible's candle amber #F3BE65 in hue and is slightly more saturated; the concept's glow is a little more orange (side lens mid tone around #C36E28). Lit engine brass sits at hue 32 to 37, saturation 0.46 to 0.58, close to the concept's lit brass (#8F6D48, hue 31, saturation 0.50). Still missing: the ruby accent (#93212B in the bible).

At about 2.6 m the hound reads as a low brass dog, distinct from the upright roster, and the face now has visible amber eyes. The chest shows three similar amber blobs instead of one focal core, so the hit-reaction light has no single point to read.

topFixes: Make the grille core the single focal light, as the art bible requires: enlarge the lit panel behind the grille bars and make it brighter than the side lenses, and shrink or dim the side lenses so they read only from the side, as in the concept. The colour half of the earlier fix is done.

Restore the ruby bosses on the shoulders and thighs through COLOR_0 on a factor material, as the warden's planets and the escapement's sapphires do, or merge the two brass sets to free a material slot.
Reshape the head into a shorter, broader greyhound skull with folded rose ears, and give the legs angled hocks with tapered, engraved forearm plates.
independentScore.method: Independent visual review against assets-source/concepts/hound-sheet-1.png by a separate reviewer agent, re-scored after the glow fix in commit ab14b81 with the geometry unchanged. Judged the concept at native resolution against the side, front and back orthographic compare, the owner review sheet (including its five engine thumbnails), the low 3/4 Blender render, the attack engine shot for pose, and the new engine shots p6-glow-spring-hound.jpg and the spring-hound row of p6-glow-before-after.jpg (before, after and frozen). Glow colour was measured as sRGB with Pillow: 5x5 median samples on each lens, the grille gaps and each eye in p6-glow-spring-hound.jpg, and the median of all pixels with saturation above 0.6 and value above 0.85 in the after crop, compared with the same pixels in the before crop. Same rubric as the previous review: silhouette and proportions 30, signature features 25, surface detail and material read 20, colour and value 15, readability at play distance 10.
